issues.title: Engine Oil Dilution from Fuel
issues.description: The 1.5L turbo engine can experience fuel mixing with engine oil during cold weather operation or short trips. This raises oil levels and reduces lubrication effectiveness. Honda extended the powertrain warranty and released software updates to address this.
issues.solution: Visit a Honda dealer for the free ECU software update that adjusts fuel injection timing. Check oil level regularly and change oil more frequently (every 3,000-5,000 miles). Avoid short trips in cold weather when possible, or let the engine fully warm up before shutting off.
symptoms: Oil level rising above full mark
Check engine light for misfire codes

issues.title: Dashboard Melting/Stickiness
issues.description: Dashboard surface can become sticky or appear to melt in hot climates. This is a cosmetic issue that doesn't affect vehicle operation but can be unsightly and cause reflections on the windshield.
issues.solution: Use a quality dashboard cover or sunshade to prevent UV damage. For existing stickiness, clean with isopropyl alcohol and apply a matte dashboard protectant. Severe cases may require dealer dashboard replacement under goodwill warranty or out-of-pocket.

issues.title: Spark Plug Thread Blowout
issues.description: The aluminum cylinder heads on Triton V8 engines have only 4 threads for spark plugs instead of the standard 8-10. This can cause spark plugs to blow out of the head, damaging threads. Helicoil repair kits are available.
issues.solution: If not yet blown out: Use anti-seize compound on spark plug threads, torque to spec (11-15 ft-lbs), and change plugs every 30k miles. If blown out: Install a Helicoil or Time-Sert thread repair kit ($50-150 DIY, $150-500 at shop). Preventive repair kits are also available to reinforce threads before failure.

issues.title: HEMI Lifter/MDS Tick
issues.description: HEMI engines with Multi-Displacement System (MDS) can develop a ticking noise from the hydraulic lifters. This is often related to the MDS deactivation system. Some owners disable MDS via tuner to eliminate the issue.
issues.solution: Try a high-quality synthetic oil (0W-40 or 5W-40) with ZDDP additive. An MDS delete kit ($200-400) permanently keeps all 8 cylinders active and eliminates the tick. Alternatively, a performance tuner ($400-600) can disable MDS via software. For severe cases, lifter replacement ($1,500-2,500) may be needed.
symptoms: Tick goes away when engine warms up
Tick more prominent on cold start

communityRecommendations.content: Many owners switched to Pennzoil Ultra Platinum 0W-40 and reported the tick went away
DiabloSport Predator tuner lets you disable MDS without hardware changes
Let the engine fully warm up before hard driving - the tick usually disappears once oil pressure stabilizes
Don't ignore severe ticking - it can lead to lifter collapse and engine damage if left untreated

issues.title: OEM Radiator Premature Failure
issues.description: The factory plastic-tank radiators on HEMI Challengers are prone to cracking and leaking, especially under track use or in hot climates. The crimped plastic end tanks can fail at the seams. Many owners report needing multiple radiator replacements.
issues.solution: Replace with an all-aluminum aftermarket radiator for long-term reliability. Mishimoto, Champion, and CSF offer direct-fit aluminum radiators with lifetime warranties. Also inspect radiator hoses and clamps during replacement. Consider adding a larger fan or oil cooler if tracking the car.
symptoms: Green or orange puddles under front of car

communityRecommendations.content: Mishimoto all-aluminum radiator - direct fit, never have to replace again
CSF Racing Radiator - excellent for track use, high flow design
Skip the OEM replacement - the plastic tanks will fail again. Go aluminum once and forget about it
If tracking your car, add a transmission cooler too - the trans runs hot with the stock setup

issues.title: Active Fuel Management Lifter Failure
issues.description: GM's Active Fuel Management (AFM) system deactivates cylinders to improve fuel economy, but can cause premature lifter wear and failure. Symptoms include rough idle, misfires, and valve train noise. GM released updated lifters.
issues.solution: Install an AFM disabler device ($100-200) to keep all cylinders active. For failed lifters: replace with updated GM lifters and consider AFM delete kit ($300-500) which includes non-AFM lifters, valley cover, and plug. Complete repair with AFM delete runs $2,000-3,500 at a shop.

issues.title: Head Gasket Failure
issues.description: The 2.5L non-turbo engine is known for external head gasket leaks. Oil seeps past the gasket and can contaminate the coolant. Subaru extended warranties and improved gasket design in later years.
issues.solution: Replace head gaskets with updated MLS (multi-layer steel) gaskets. Ensure the machine shop resurfaces cylinder heads to proper flatness. Replace timing belt, water pump, and thermostat while engine is apart. Use Subaru coolant conditioner to help prevent future failures. Budget $1,500-2,500 for a quality repair.

issues.title: CVT Transmission Failure
issues.description: Nissan's Continuously Variable Transmission (CVT) in this generation can experience premature failure. Symptoms include shuddering, hesitation, and complete transmission failure. Nissan extended CVT warranty to 10 years/120,000 miles.
issues.solution: Check if your vehicle is covered under Nissan's extended CVT warranty (10 years/120,000 miles). Change CVT fluid every 30,000 miles with Nissan NS-3 fluid only. Avoid aggressive driving and heavy towing. If warranty expired, rebuilt CVT costs $2,500-3,500, new unit $4,000-5,000.
symptoms: Check engine light with transmission codes

issues.title: TIPM (Fuse Box) Failure
issues.description: The Totally Integrated Power Module (TIPM) can fail, causing various electrical issues including fuel pump relay problems (no start), random horn honking, and erratic behavior of lights and accessories.
issues.solution: For fuel pump relay failure: Install an external bypass relay kit ($30-50 DIY) to power fuel pump directly. For complete fix: Replace TIPM unit with remanufactured unit ($400-600) or new OEM ($800-1,200). Some electrical shops can repair/rebuild existing TIPM for $200-400.

issues.title: High Pressure Fuel Pump (HPFP) Failure
issues.description: The N54 twin-turbo engine's high pressure fuel pump can fail, causing long cranking, rough idle, and power loss. BMW extended warranty coverage and released updated pump designs.
issues.solution: Check VIN with BMW dealer for extended warranty coverage (10 years/120,000 miles on HPFP). Replace with updated revision HPFP (part numbers ending in higher revision letters). Use only Top Tier gasoline. DIY replacement possible with special tools ($500-800 parts), shop labor adds $200-400.
symptoms: Check engine light with fuel pressure codes

issues.title: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure
issues.description: The timing chain tensioner can fail, causing the chain to skip timing. VW updated the tensioner design in later production. A failed tensioner can lead to catastrophic engine damage if not addressed.
issues.solution: Replace timing chain, tensioner, and guides with updated parts (revision K or later tensioner). Check for stretched chain using VW diagnostic tool. Repair should include chain, tensioner, guides, and related seals. Cost is $1,500-3,000 depending on shop. Catch it early - a skipped chain can destroy the engine.

issues.title: Theta II Engine Seizure/Failure
issues.description: The Theta II engine can seize due to metal debris blocking oil flow to connecting rod bearings. Hyundai issued recalls and extended warranties. Affected engines may need replacement.
issues.solution: Check VIN for active recalls - Hyundai provides free engine replacement for affected vehicles. Install the knock sensor detection system (KSDS) software update that monitors for bearing wear. Change oil every 5,000 miles. If engine fails and under warranty, replacement is free. Out of warranty replacement: $4,000-8,000.

issues.title: Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves
issues.description: Direct injection engines like the Skyactiv can develop carbon buildup on intake valves since fuel doesn't wash over them. This can cause rough idle and reduced performance. Walnut blasting is the common fix.
issues.solution: Have intake valves walnut blasted every 60,000-80,000 miles ($300-600). Use a quality intake cleaner like CRC GDI IVD Intake Valve Cleaner periodically. Consider adding a catch can to reduce oil vapor entering the intake. Use Top Tier gasoline for better detergent content.
symptoms: Check engine light for misfire codes
